exercises.en: It might snow tomorrow.
exercises.why: 어쩌면 pairs with ~ㄹ/을지도 모르다, and 오다 takes ㄹ지도 because it ends in a vowel.

exercises.ko: ___ 오늘은 집에 늦게 갈 것 같아요.
exercises.en: After thinking it over, I'll probably go home late today.
exercises.why: 아무래도 + ~ㄹ/을 것 같다 means 'probably', after weighing things up.

exercises.en: How old is your grandfather?
exercises.why: 연세 is the respectful word for age used for elderly people.

exercises.en: I'm going to go see my teacher tomorrow.
exercises.why: The stem 뵈 takes 러 directly; 봬 is only the contraction of 뵈어.

exercises.en: See you next week, teacher.
exercises.why: 뵈 + 어요 contracts to 봬요, just like 되 + 어요 becomes 돼요.

exercises.en: My mother tends a small garden in front of the house.
exercises.why: 가꾸 + 어요 merges into 가꿔요.

exercises.en: My younger sibling went to the convenience store in pajamas.
exercises.why: Clothing + 차림으로 says what someone is dressed in while doing something.

exercises.en: My birthday is next Friday, that is, the 10th.
exercises.why: 즉 introduces a restatement: 'that is' or 'in other words'.

exercises.en: Maybe my friend is at home now.
exercises.ko: 어쩌면 친구가 지금 집에 있을지도 몰라요.

exercises.en: It looks like the bus will probably be late.
My grandfather is eighty years old. (respectful)
My friend came out in exercise clothes.

reading.ko: 이번 주말에 할머니를 뵈러 대구에 가요. 할머니는 연세가 많으시지만 아직 건강하세요. 할머니는 집 앞에서 채소와 꽃을 가꾸세요. 지난번에 저는 운동복 차림으로 할머니 집에 갔어요. 그래서 이번에는 예쁜 옷을 입을 거예요. 어쩌면 오빠도 같이 갈지도 몰라요. 아무래도 이번 주말은 아주 바쁠 것 같아요.
reading.en: This weekend I'm going to Daegu to see my grandmother. My grandmother is elderly, but she is still healthy. She grows vegetables and flowers in front of her house. Last time I went to her house in exercise clothes. So this time I'm going to wear nice clothes. Maybe my older brother will come with me too. This weekend will probably be very busy.

questions.q: 지난번에 이 사람은 어떤 옷차림으로 갔어요?

exercises.en: The subway is packed with people.
exercises.why: What fills a space takes (으)로, and a noun ending in ㄹ takes 로.

exercises.en: The cup is full of water.
exercises.why: 차다 + 아 있다 becomes 차 있다, a state of being full.

exercises.en: For some reason I'm not in a good mood today.
exercises.why: 왠지 (from 왜 그런지) means 'for some reason'; 웬지 is a common misspelling.

exercises.en: Don't tell me you already finished all your homework?
exercises.why: 설마 at the start of a question shows you can hardly believe it.

exercises.en: Please stamp your seal on this paper.
exercises.why: 찍다 takes its 아/어 form before 주세요.

exercises.ko: 비가 오기 전에 집에 도착___ 다행이에요.
exercises.en: Thankfully I got home before it rained.
exercises.why: ~아/어서 다행이다 expresses relief that something happened.

exercises.en: Fortunately I found my wallet.
exercises.why: The adverb form is 다행히, 'fortunately'.

exercises.en: My friend is coming to Korea sometime in December.
exercises.why: Month + 달에 means 'sometime in that month', and time takes 에.

exercises.en: The bag is full of books.
For some reason I want to eat Korean food today.
exercises.ko: 오늘은 왠지 한국 음식을 먹고 싶어요.

exercises.en: Thankfully it didn't rain.
Could you take a picture of me?

reading.ko: 토요일에 친구와 같이 공원에 갔어요. 공원은 사람들로 가득 찼어요. 우리는 꽃 앞에서 사진을 많이 찍었어요. 그런데 집에 왔을 때 카메라가 없었어요. 저는 친구에게 전화했어요. 다행히 친구가 제 카메라를 가지고 있었어요. 카메라를 찾아서 정말 다행이에요. 우리는 5월 달에 다시 공원에 갈 거예요.
reading.en: On Saturday I went to the park with a friend. The park was packed with people. We took lots of photos in front of the flowers. But when I got home, I didn't have my camera. I called my friend. Fortunately my friend had my camera. I'm really relieved I found it. We're going to the park again sometime in May.

exercises.en: I hope you are all happy.
exercises.why: 바라다 takes a clause nominalised with ~기(를); 시 adds respect.

exercises.en: I hope only good things happen.
exercises.why: Before 바라다, the verb becomes a noun with ~기를.

exercises.en: Please turn off your phones before class. (formal announcement)
exercises.why: ~아/어 주시기 바랍니다 is a formal request in announcements.

exercises.en: I hope the weather is nice tomorrow.
exercises.why: ~았/었으면 좋겠다 is a fixed unit for wishes, even about the future.

exercises.en: I wish vacation would come soon.
exercises.why: 오 + 았으면 contracts to 왔으면.

exercises.en: I wish I had a little more time.
exercises.why: 있다 takes 었으면 because its last vowel is not ㅏ or ㅗ.

exercises.en: I wish Dad would come pick me up at the station.
exercises.why: 데리러 오다 means 'to come pick someone up'.

exercises.en: I hope everything goes well.
exercises.why: ~기 ends in a vowel, so the object marker is 를.

exercises.en: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
Grandmother, I hope you stay healthy. (formal)
I wish I were a twin.
Please do your best. (formal request)

reading.ko: 제 동생들은 쌍둥이예요. 다음 주에 동생들이 큰 시험을 봐요. 동생들은 요즘 밤까지 열심히 공부해요. 저는 동생들이 최선을 다했으면 좋겠어요. 시험이 끝나면 제가 학교로 동생들을 데리러 갈 거예요. 그리고 같이 맛있는 음식을 먹었으면 좋겠어요. 동생들에게 좋은 결과가 있기를 바라요.
reading.en: My younger siblings are twins. Next week they have a big exam. These days they study hard until night. I hope they do their best. When the exam is over, I'll go to the school to pick them up. And I hope we can eat delicious food together. I hope they get good results.

questions.q: 시험이 끝나면 이 사람은 뭘 할 거예요?
이 사람은 동생들에게 뭐가 있기를 바라요?

exercises.en: I exercise while listening to music.
exercises.why: 듣다 is ㄷ irregular, so it becomes 들으면서.

exercises.en: I walked while talking with my friend.
exercises.why: A vowel stem takes ~면서 directly.

exercises.en: He learned Korean while living in Seoul.
exercises.why: An ㄹ stem takes ~면서 directly, with no 으.

exercises.en: I sat on a chair and read a book.
exercises.why: Posture verbs use ~아/어서; 앉으면서 would mean 'while sitting down'.

exercises.en: This bag is cheap and light at the same time.
exercises.why: With adjectives, ~(으)면서 joins two qualities at once.

exercises.en: My friend is a student and an office worker at the same time.
exercises.why: After a consonant, 이다 becomes 이면서.

exercises.en: He was full, yet he ate ramen again.
exercises.why: ~(으)면서도 links two clashing facts: 'even though'.

exercises.en: This park is spacious and quiet. (formal writing)
exercises.why: ~(으)며 links clauses in formal writing, and a consonant stem takes 으며.

exercises.en: I read a book while drinking tea.
I grew up watching Korean dramas.
Today it's cloudy and windy.
He says he has no money, yet he buys souvenirs every day.
exercises.ko: 그는 돈이 없다고 하면서 매일 기념품을 사요.

reading.ko: 저는 지난달에 부산을 여행했어요. 부산은 바다가 아름다우면서 음식도 맛있어요. 저는 바다를 보면서 커피를 마셨어요. 관광객들이 바다 앞에서 사진을 찍으며 웃고 있었어요. 저도 동영상을 많이 찍었어요. 그리고 친구들에게 줄 기념품을 샀어요. 일정이 바빴지만 정말 즐거웠어요.
reading.en: Last month I traveled to Busan. Busan has a beautiful sea and tasty food too. I drank coffee while looking at the sea. Tourists were laughing while taking pictures in front of the sea. I took lots of videos too. And I bought souvenirs to give to my friends. The schedule was busy, but it was really fun.

questions.q: 이 사람은 바다를 보면서 뭘 했어요?
이 사람은 친구들에게 뭘 줄 거예요?

exercises.en: Where shall we eat dinner?
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을까요? suggests doing something together; 먹다 has a consonant stem, so 을까요.

exercises.en: Shall I carry your bag for you?
exercises.why: ~아/어 드릴까요? politely offers to do something for someone.

exercises.en: I'll contact you again tomorrow.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을게요 is a promise; it is spelled 게 even though it sounds like 께.

exercises.en: I'll read this book.
exercises.why: A consonant stem takes 을게요 for 'I'll do it'.

exercises.en: What should I make tonight? (thinking to myself, casual)
exercises.why: An ㄹ stem just adds ㄹ까, so 만들다 becomes 만들까.

exercises.en: Do you think he has already arrived home?
exercises.why: ~았/었을까요? guesses about something that may already have happened.

exercises.en: How about leaving tomorrow morning?
exercises.why: 어떻다 + ㄹ까요 becomes 어떨까요, a gentle way to suggest something.

exercises.en: Do you think that movie will be fun?
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을까요? asks the listener's opinion about how likely something is.

exercises.en: Shall we take a taxi?
Shall I turn on the light?
I'll wait here.
Do you think it will be cold tomorrow?

reading.ko: 민수: 토요일에 같이 영화 볼까요? 지수: 좋아요. 몇 시에 만날까요? 민수: 세 시는 어떨까요? 지수: 좋아요. 그런데 표가 있을까요? 민수: 제가 오늘 밤에 표를 살게요. 지수: 고마워요. 그러면 제가 팝콘을 살게요.
reading.en: Minsu: Shall we watch a movie together on Saturday? Jisu: Sounds good. What time shall we meet? Minsu: How about three o'clock? Jisu: Good. But do you think there will be tickets? Minsu: I'll buy the tickets tonight. Jisu: Thanks. Then I'll buy the popcorn.

questions.q: 민수와 지수는 토요일에 뭘 할 거예요?

exercises.en: I'm thinking of going to Jeju Island this vacation.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을까 하다 states a tentative plan: 'I'm thinking of...'.

exercises.en: I'm thinking of eating ramen at home this evening.
exercises.why: A consonant stem takes 을까 before 하다.

exercises.en: I was thinking of buying new clothes, so I went to the department store.
exercises.why: Mid-sentence, use ~ㄹ/을까 해서 to mean 'I was thinking of..., so'.

exercises.en: I think I might take a walk in the park this evening.
exercises.why: 걷다 is ㄷ irregular, so it becomes 걸을까.

exercises.ko: 어제 친구를 ___ 했는데 너무 피곤해서 그냥 집에 있었어요.
exercises.en: I was thinking of meeting a friend yesterday, but I was so tired I just stayed home.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을까 했다 means you considered it but didn't do it.

exercises.en: I was thinking of taking the bus, but the weather was nice so I walked.
exercises.why: Past 했는데 shows a plan you considered and then dropped.

exercises.en: Last year I was thinking of changing my name, but I didn't.
exercises.why: A vowel stem takes ㄹ까 before 하다.

exercises.en: I'm thinking of starting to exercise this winter.
exercises.why: 시작하 + ㄹ까 해요 states a tentative plan.

exercises.en: I'm thinking of going to the movie theater tonight.
I think I might stay two nights in Busan.
I was thinking of calling my mother, but it was too late.
I'm thinking of looking at the weather forecast first.

reading.ko: 이번 가을에 단풍 구경을 갈까 해요. 처음에는 북부에 있는 큰 산에 갈까 했는데 너무 멀어요. 그래서 남부에 있는 산에 갈까 봐요. 거기에서 1박을 할까 해요. 그런데 기상예보에서 주말에 이슬비가 온다고 했어요. 그래도 저는 우산을 가지고 갈 거예요. 단풍을 보면서 사진을 많이 찍고 싶어요.
reading.en: This autumn I'm thinking of going to see the autumn leaves. At first I was thinking of going to a big mountain in the north, but it's too far. So I think I might go to a mountain in the south. I'm thinking of staying one night there. But the weather forecast said it will drizzle on the weekend. Even so, I'll take an umbrella and go. I want to take lots of photos while looking at the leaves.

questions.q: 이 사람은 이번 가을에 뭘 할까 해요?
왜 북부에 있는 산에 안 가요?

exercises.en: I'm worried I'll be late for the meeting.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을까 봐 걱정되다 means 'I'm worried that...'.

exercises.en: I was worried it would be cold, so I wore warm clothes.
exercises.why: 춥다 is ㅂ irregular, so it becomes 추울까.

exercises.en: I was worried I'd get lost, so I took a map.
exercises.why: The tense goes on the final verb, so the verb before ~ㄹ/을까 봐 stays non-past.

exercises.ko: 친구가 제 문자를 못 ___ 봐 걱정돼요.
exercises.en: I'm worried my friend might not have seen my text.
exercises.why: For something that may already have happened, use ~았/었을까 봐.

exercises.ko: 동생이 ___ 봐 불을 끄고 조용히 나갔어요.
exercises.en: I was worried my younger sibling would wake up, so I turned off the light and quietly went out.
exercises.why: A vowel stem takes ㄹ까 봐.

exercises.en: I'm worried it might snow a lot tomorrow.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을까 봐요 alone can mean worry, with 걱정되다 dropped.

exercises.en: I was worried my words might have been rude.
exercises.why: ~았/었을까 봐 worries about something that may already be true.

exercises.en: I'm worried the landlord will think we're rude.
exercises.why: 생각하 + ㄹ까 봐 says what you fear might happen.

exercises.en: I'm worried the bus might not come.
I studied hard because I was worried I'd fail the exam.
I'm worried the roof might break.
I closed the window because I was worried my younger sibling would catch a cold.
exercises.ko: 동생이 감기에 걸릴까 봐 창문을 닫았어요.

reading.ko: 저는 요즘 논문을 쓰고 있어요. 다음 달까지 논문을 끝내야 돼요. 그런데 시간이 부족할까 봐 걱정돼요. 그래서 주말에도 도서관에서 작업해요. 어제는 친구가 제 논문을 읽어 줬어요. 친구가 '글쎄요, 조금 길어요.'라고 했어요. 그래서 논문을 조금 짧게 바꿨어요.
reading.en: These days I'm writing my thesis. I have to finish it by next month. But I'm worried there won't be enough time. So I work in the library even on weekends. Yesterday my friend read my thesis for me. My friend said, 'Well... it's a bit long.' So I made the thesis a little shorter.

questions.q: 이 사람은 왜 주말에도 도서관에서 작업해요?

exercises.en: I've almost finished writing the letter.
exercises.why: 거의 다 means 'almost all', for an action nearly finished.

exercises.en: I almost missed the bus this morning.
exercises.why: 뻔했다 always follows the future modifier ~ㄹ/을.

exercises.en: It hurt so much that I almost cried.
exercises.why: An ㄹ stem already ends in ㄹ, so 울다 becomes 울 뻔했어요.

exercises.en: I overslept and was almost late for class.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을 뻔하다 is almost always used in the past: 뻔했어요.

exercises.en: The food was so spicy I almost died.
exercises.why: A consonant stem takes 을 before 뻔했다.

exercises.en: I almost crossed the road on a red light.
exercises.why: 건너다 has a vowel stem, so it takes ㄹ before 뻔했다.

exercises.en: My older sister and I are almost the same height.
exercises.why: 거의 같다 means 'almost the same'; 전혀 and 별로 need a negative.

exercises.en: The button on my shirt almost came off.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을 뻔했다 says something almost happened but didn't.

exercises.en: I've almost finished my coffee.
I almost forgot my friend's birthday.
I almost lost my wallet.
I almost fell asleep in class.

reading.ko: 어제는 정말 힘든 날이었어요. 아침에 늦잠을 자서 지하철을 놓칠 뻔했어요. 다행히 회사에 늦지 않았어요. 점심에는 셔츠 단추가 떨어질 뻔했어요. 저녁에 집에 갈 때는 계단에서 넘어질 뻔했어요. 집에 도착했을 때 거의 열한 시였어요. 저는 씻고 바로 잤어요.
reading.en: Yesterday was a really hard day. I overslept in the morning and almost missed the subway. Fortunately I wasn't late for work. At lunch my shirt button almost came off. In the evening, on my way home, I almost fell on the stairs. When I got home it was almost eleven o'clock. I washed up and went straight to bed.
